messages:
rachel: quick follow-up from the autoscale RFC: i've been thinking about a borrow-first flow where small local buffers absorb microbursts and only then request from a shared reservoir. pros/cons?

tom: borrow-first reduces global churn and keeps latency tight for short bursts. downside: accounting is trickier and we need visible degradation paths.

anika: agree. important to separate admission vs billing: admission should be fast and local; billing events can be emitted async with strong order guarantees.

infra-bot: alert: shared_reservoir_util=88% at 2026-03-02T11:03:12Z

rachel: runtime implication: operator should manage borrow tokens with decay and hard caps. CP should only publish commit + borrow_budget per tenant. operator maps budget->local_buffer_size.

tom: propose config sample for the spike prototype:
```
borrow_policy:
  local_buffer_tokens: 3000
  borrow_decay_half_life_s: 45
  hard_borrow_cap: 20000
  reservoir_spill_threshold_pct: 85
  grace_window_ms: 500
```

anika: observability: require per-tenant traces for borrow events, reclaim events, and fallback routing counts. add alerts when borrow_charge_latency > 2s.

rachel: rollout plan: 1) sim with heavy-tail tenants, 2) k8s operator PoC with opt-in alpha tenants, 3) small canary route for non-critical customers. watch reservoir_util and borrowed_token_rate.

tom: i'll own the PoC. anika, can you own dashboards? rachel i'll draft the short RFC with config + metrics.

anika: yes. add a test for adversarial microburst patterns so we can validate EWMA caps.

infra-bot: note: follow-up task created: autoscale/borrow-poc assigned to tom.

rachel: thanks all, decision for now: prototype borrow-first local buffer + shared reservoir, operator-owned sizing & admission; CP stays minimal. will capture in RFC. :white_check_mark:
